standard_prerequisites.name: For a flat ring map A to B and a complex of B-modules that is flat over A, the derived tensor product with a B-module agrees with the ordinary tensor product, and localization at a prime of B is computed through the residue field of the prime below
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies replacing the derived tensors over A and over B by ordinary ones and the displayed chain of identifications for K tensor^L_B kappa(q).

core_obligations: Reduce to a bounded above complex K of finite free B-modules, which is then flat over A and for which K tensor_A M equals the derived tensor product with M, so that the hypothesis on tor amplitude may be used through ordinary tensor products (proof lines 20190-20195).

For each prime p of A, note that K tensor_A kappa(p) is a bounded above complex of finite free modules over B tensor_A kappa(p) whose cohomology vanishes outside the interval from a to b, and apply the finite global dimension hypothesis to conclude that it has tor amplitude in [a - d, b] (proof lines 20195-20205).

For a prime q of B lying over p, compute K tensor^L_B kappa(q) as (K tensor_A kappa(p)) tensor over B tensor_A kappa(p) with kappa(q), using flatness of K over A to replace the derived tensor products by ordinary ones and to identify the base changes (proof lines 20206-20216).

Conclude from that identification and from the previous estimate that H^i(K tensor^L_B kappa(q)) vanishes for i outside [a - d, b] for every prime q of B, and apply the fibrewise criterion for perfectness to obtain that K is perfect with tor amplitude in [a - d, b] (proof lines 20217-20220).
proof_roadmap: Replace the pseudo-coherent complex by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and record that it is then flat over A (proof lines 20190-20195).
Estimate the fibre over each prime of A using the finite global dimension assumption, obtaining tor amplitude [a - d, b] over the fibrewise rings (proof lines 20195-20205).
Rewrite the fibre over a prime of B in terms of the fibre over the prime of A below it and propagate the vanishing of the cohomology to all primes of B (proof lines 20206-20216).
Apply the fibrewise criterion for perfectness to conclude (proof lines 20217-20220).
difficulty_reason: The statement takes a flat ring map A -> B whose fibres B tensor_A kappa(p) all have global dimension at most d, and a pseudo-coherent complex K of B-modules with tor amplitude in [a, b] over A, and concludes that K is perfect over B with tor amplitude in the shifted range [a - d, b] (statement lines 20174-20188). The proof has to move the estimate from the fibres over primes of A to the fibres over primes of B: after replacing K by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, which makes it flat over A, the fibrewise bound over A is obtained from the finite global dimension hypothesis, and the fibre over a prime q of B is then computed by base changing the fibre over the prime below it along the fibrewise ring map, using the displayed chain of identifications (proof lines 20190-20216). The two cited results are the fibrewise tor amplitude estimate and the fibrewise criterion for perfectness, and the computation that connects them is inside the counted span.
